players.product: hyperscale data-center leases (>1 MW, 300+ data centers, 1.4 GW under construction) and 0-1 MW colocation / interconnection on PlatformDIGITAL

quarterly_data.signal: Record quarter: core FFO excluding net promote income $2.13 per share, +14% YoY (reported core FFO $2.65 including a $0.52 promote from the Blackstone transaction); same-capital cash NOI +8.9% YoY (+7.2% constant currency). 2026 core FFO per share guidance (ex promote) raised to $8.15-$8.20, implying 10% constant-currency growth at the midpoint, a second consecutive year of double-digit growth.
quarterly_data.figure: core FFO ex-promote $2.13/share (+14% YoY); 2026 core FFO guidance $8.15-$8.20/share; same-capital cash NOI +8.9%

quarterly_data.signal: Total backlog reached a record $1.9 billion of annualized rent at 100% share ($1.4 billion at Digital Realty share, up 75% since the beginning of the year), roughly 30% of in-place data center rent, before the $410 million of hyperscale leases signed in July. $208 million of rent commenced in Q2; $635 million is scheduled to commence in 2H 2026 (45% in Q3, 55% in Q4), $480 million in 2027 and $312 million in 2028 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: record backlog $1.9B annualized rent (100% share) / $1.4B DLR share (+75% YTD); $635M commencing 2H 2026, $480M in 2027, $312M in 2028+

quarterly_data.signal: Hyperscale leasing: two additional U.S. hyperscale leases signed just after quarter end for approximately $410 million of annualized GAAP rent at 100% share ($205 million at DLR share); about $1.4 billion of hyperscale signings in the first half plus early July, already eclipsing all of last year's total signings. Q1's 200 MW Charlotte lease was the largest in company history. Over the last 10 quarters the top signing came from six different top hyperscalers across six markets; large-footprint capacity is still booked with traditional investment-grade hyperscalers, not neoclouds.
quarterly_data.figure: $410M annualized rent from two hyperscale leases signed in July ($205M DLR share); ~$1.4B hyperscale signings YTD incl. July; 200 MW Charlotte lease

quarterly_data.signal: Development pipeline: 1.4 GW under construction at a total cost of $20 billion (a 100% increase during 1H 2026), 63% pre-leased pro forma the July leases at an 11.5% expected stabilized yield; more than 80% of it in the Americas. 312 MW of new starts in Q2 (Northern Virginia, Marseille) and 76 MW delivered (~60% pre-leased). The 1.4 GW is a ~45% expansion on just over 3 GW operating today, within a 9 GW growth runway; close to 1.5 GW of 2027-2028 deliveries are in active customer dialogue.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.4 GW under construction at $20B total cost, 63% pre-leased, 11.5% yield; ~3 GW operating; 9 GW runway; 312 MW of new starts in Q2

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 CapEx guidance (net of partner contributions) increased by $750 million from last quarter to $4.25 billion-$4.75 billion, 'driven by our recent leasing success and the strong demand outlook'; another $500 million added to dispositions / JV capital guidance to fund it.

Invested $1.1 billion in development CapEx during the quarter, net of partners' share, bringing year-to-date capital spending to $2 billion; land acquired in Kansas City, Marseille and Atlanta plus operating and development assets in Malaysia.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 development CapEx $1.1B (net of partners); YTD $2B

quarterly_data.signal: Kansas City expansion: secured 600 MW of utility power that begins to ramp in early 2028 (linear from there) with a long-term runway of up to 2 GW across over 1,400 acres; market has 25+ network providers, <10 ms latency to more than 50% of the U.S. population, and several hyperscaler self-build deployments already underway; construction expected to begin in 2H 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 600 MW of utility power secured in Kansas City ramping from 2028; runway up to 2 GW over 1,400 acres

quarterly_data.signal: Acquired Blackstone's blended 64% equity interest in three fully leased Northern Virginia hyperscale data centers totaling 288 MW of IT capacity for $1.2 billion in cash plus 12.3 million shares (~$2.3 billion), assuming the partner's share of a $725 million loan; first two facilities stabilize in 1H 2027, the third in 1H 2028. Continuing to partner with Blackstone on the remaining 400 MW+ in the development venture; roughly $200 million of promote income realized.
quarterly_data.figure: 288 MW of fully leased Northern Virginia hyperscale capacity acquired (64% interest) for $1.2B cash + 12.3M shares (~$2.3B); 400 MW+ remains in JV

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing power from supply-demand imbalance: over $261 million of renewals signed with cash re-leasing spreads over 25% (0-1 MW 5.2%; greater-than-1 MW 66.7%, strongest in Singapore); 2026 cash renewal spread guidance raised to 9%-11%. Record $108 million of 0-1 MW plus interconnection bookings (third consecutive record; AI-related wins roughly 20% of it) and record $20.5 million of interconnection bookings.
quarterly_data.figure: renewal cash spreads >25% (>1 MW: 66.7%); 2026 spread guide 9%-11%; record 0-1 MW bookings $108M (AI ~20%); interconnection bookings $20.5M

quarterly_data.signal: Funding capacity: $3.25 billion U.S. Hyperscale Fund closed earlier this year (about $10 billion of total spend capacity with leverage); over $12 billion of remaining capacity to support hyperscale development including the JV dry powder; agreed to acquire Columbia Capital (~$485 million, $9 billion+ of fund commitments) and a 16% interest in Teraco (~$650 million). Leverage 4.7x debt/EBITDA with ~$6 billion of liquidity.
quarterly_data.figure: $3.25B U.S. Hyperscale Fund; >$12B remaining hyperscale development capacity; leverage 4.7x; ~$6B liquidity
